gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the unsupported replacement of the fixed-n_2 inner limit based on cover counts by a supremum of ratios based on exact-spectrum cover counts. They specifically recognize that the factor-three estimate establishes only equality of the eventual outer limsup, not the displayed fixed-n_2 equality.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The proof invalidly equates the fixed-n_2 inner limit of quantities involving N_{\delta_k}(\Gamma_{n(\delta_k)}^\spec(A)) with the corresponding supremum using N_{\delta_k}(\spec(A)); the available factor-three comparison does not give that equality.

component_coverage.gold_component: The fixed-n_2 inner-limit equality replaces cover counts for the approximating spectral neighborhoods by exact-spectrum cover counts, although only a factor-three comparison and an outer-limsup relation are justified.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states that the inner limit must use cover counts, that the factor-three estimate gives only the same eventual limsup rather than fixed-n_2 equality, and proposes the corresponding corrected proof strategy.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns the false assumption that finite-support coupling implies finite graph degree, which makes the breadth-first finite-neighbor construction undefined for an infinite star. ISSUE-005 instead concerns unsupported numerical claims about spectral pollution and one-sided distance estimates; it does not recognize the graph-local-finiteness obligation or the failure of the breadth-first construction.
